input: Write a due diligence memo on Deel

team.claim: Official leadership page observed 2026-11-09 lists co-founders Alex Bouaziz as CEO and Shuo Wang as CRO.

Official leadership page observed 2026-11-09 lists Joe Kauffman, president/CFO; Dan Westgarth, COO; Philippe Bouaziz, executive chairman/chief strategy officer; Yaron Lavi, CTO; Harish Sharma, chief risk officer; DeAnn Work, global corporate general counsel; and Anthony Rodriguez, chief compliance officer.
Company biographies observed 2026-11-09 say Alex Bouaziz previously co-founded Sarona Ventures; Shuo Wang co-founded Aeris Cleantec and served as CTO until its acquisition by iRobot.

Company announcement dated 2025-11-03: Joe Kauffman joined as president/CFO after serving as CFO, president and CEO at Credit Karma. Founding CFO Philippe Bouaziz moved to executive chairman/chief strategy officer rather than departing.

TechCrunch reported on 2025-04-05 that communications head Elisabeth Diana had departed; Deel acknowledged her contribution. The report places the exit amid the Rippling dispute but does not establish that the dispute caused her departure.

funding.claim: Historical primary-source disclosure: $14 million Series A closed in May 2020, led by Andreessen Horowitz; $30 million Series B announced 2020-09-09, led by Spark Capital.
Company announcement dated 2021-04-21: $156 million Series C at a $1.25 billion valuation, led by YC Continuity Fund and co-led by existing investors Andreessen Horowitz and Spark Capital.
Company announcement dated 2021-10-18: $425 million Series D at a $5.5 billion valuation, led by Coatue.

Axios reported on 2022-05-11 a $50 million financing at a $12 billion valuation, with Emerson Collective among new investors. Deel and Emerson declined comment; the article does not identify a lead investor.

Company claim dated 2025-04-30: General Catalyst and an unnamed sovereign investor purchased close to $300 million in secondary shares from early investors; this was shareholder liquidity, not primary capital raised by Deel.

Latest verified priced primary round as of 2026-11-09: Reuters reported on 2025-10-16 a $300 million Series E at a $17.3 billion valuation, led by Ribbit Capital alongside Andreessen Horowitz and Coatue. This is a historical financing valuation, not a current fair-value appraisal.

output.verdict: Deel shows substantial commercial scale, a broad global product suite and strong funding access, supported by company disclosures and reporting on its latest priced round. Proceed to deeper diligence rather than an investment conclusion: prioritize audited financial reconciliation, the civil litigation and reported criminal inquiry, and security/control remediation.

business.claim: Company claim; as of 2026-11-09: sells an integrated global payroll, HR, hiring, benefits and IT platform to companies from startups to enterprise; homepage advertises coverage across 150+ countries.

Company claim; pricing observed 2026-11-09: recurring per-worker fees start at $49 per contractor per month and $599 per employer-of-record employee per month. EOR handles legal employment, contracts, payroll, benefits and compliance without the customer opening a local entity.

Company claim; pricing observed 2026-11-09 distinguishes EOR legal employment in 130+ countries from broader platform coverage; contractor-of-record service starts at $325 per contractor per month and shifts classification responsibility to Deel.

traction.claim: Company claim; homepage observed 2026-11-09 reports 40,000+ customer companies. This is a current marketing snapshot, not an independently audited customer count.
Company claim; as of 2025-11-03, served more than 37,000 businesses, versus 35,000+ reported in June 2025; customer-count definitions and retention were not disclosed.
Company claim; named customers on the about page observed 2026-11-09 include Shopify, Nike and Klarna.
Company claim; homepage observed 2026-11-09 features customer examples Robinhood, Revolut, Strada and Bowmans.
Partner announcement dated 2024-05-16: dLocal expanded its Deel payments partnership into 12 additional countries beyond the initial 19-country deployment; a payments partner, not a customer.

red_flags.claim: Governance/legal diligence priority: core espionage-related civil claims survived pleading review. Request outside-counsel assessments, litigation reserves, insurance coverage and executive conflict/oversight records; do not treat unproven allegations as established misconduct.
Reported criminal inquiry increases legal and reputational uncertainty beyond the civil litigation; independently establish current investigative/charging status before investment.
Third-party integration exposure: the disclosed Klue incident warrants review of CRM access controls, vendor token governance, notification completeness and residual phishing risk.

Financial verification gap: the company’s ARR, monthly revenue and undefined profitability claims require reconciliation to audited recognized revenue, cash generation and acquisition-adjusted organic growth before underwriting valuation.

reputation.claim: Anonymous-review aggregator snapshot observed 2026-11-09: Glassdoor showed 4.3/5 from 2,147 reviews, 84% recommending Deel and 89% CEO approval. This is self-selected employee feedback, not a representative survey; no consistent longitudinal rating trend was verified.

BBB complaint aggregator snapshot observed 2026-11-09: 17 complaints over the prior three years and eight closed in the prior twelve months. Published complaints include billing/contract disputes, including an alleged commitment-shortfall charge; allegations are not adjudicated and the sample is not a customer-wide complaint rate.

Critical press: WSJ’s 2026-01-23 report escalated the Rippling allegations from a civil competitive dispute to a reported criminal inquiry. Reporting of an investigation does not establish misconduct.

missing_fields: audited annual revenue and financial statements
cash flow, cash balance, debt and net income
gross and net revenue retention, churn and customer concentration
current valuation after the October 2025 primary round
verified comparable headcount trend and quantified layoffs through 2026-11-09
latest DOJ investigative or charging status from a public agency or court record
final Klue incident scope and regulatory outcome
litigation status after the latest opened substantive order dated 2026-09-25

financial_signals.claim: Company claim reported by Reuters on 2025-06-03: crossed $1 billion annual revenue run-rate in Q1 2025; revenue increased 75% for the twelve months ended 2025-04-30; EBITDA margin was 16% for Q1 ended 2025-03-31. Run-rate and EBITDA are not audited annual GAAP revenue or net income.

Company claim dated 2025-10-20: exceeded $1 billion ARR, recorded its first $100 million revenue month in September 2025 and marked three consecutive years of profitability that September; the announcement does not define profitability.

Third-party research estimate, not audited financials: Sacra estimates $1.5 billion annualized revenue in June 2026, up from $1.3 billion at end-2025. Page observed 2026-11-09; this estimate is distinct from recognized annual revenue.
Company claim dated 2025-06-03: 6,500+ team members across more than 100 countries. A like-for-like subsequent headcount series was not verified.

Company careers-page snapshot observed 2026-11-09 advertises 248 open positions, including sales, payroll and product/design. Postings indicate recruiting intent, not completed hires or net headcount growth.

legal_and_regulatory.claim: Court record: Rippling alleges Deel and senior executives directed a corporate-espionage scheme to obtain confidential information. On 2026-02-23, the Northern District of California largely denied dismissal motions, leaving core RICO and trade-secret claims proceeding while dismissing some state-law claims. Allegations surviving pleading review are not findings of liability.

Latest opened substantive order, 2026-09-25: the court denied Deel’s motion to strike, compelled arbitration of certain Deel counterclaims and granted in part/denied in part dismissal of counterclaims. Rippling litigation remained active in this record; this was not a merits exoneration or final judgment.

WSJ reported on 2026-01-23, citing documents and people familiar with the matter, that DOJ opened a criminal investigation into alleged spying at Rippling and issued grand-jury subpoenas. This is press-reported investigative activity, not a public charging document or conviction.
Ogletree’s 2026-03-27 discussion of the reported DOJ probe says Deel denied the allegations, said it was unaware of a criminal investigation and would cooperate with authorities.

A receiver’s complaint filed 2025-01-03 alleged unlicensed money transmission, inadequate AML/KYC controls and Russia-related sanctions evasion involving Deel. These were civil plaintiff allegations, not regulator findings; see the subsequent dismissal below.

Court order dated 2025-08-18 in Damian v. Deel: dismissed the complaint and closed the case for lack of cognizable injury/standing and failure to plead a distinct RICO enterprise. The order expressly did not address all arguments; dismissal did not adjudicate the underlying licensing/sanctions allegations as true or false.

California Senator Steve Padilla requested a labor-agency investigation on 2023-07-06 into alleged worker misclassification and client advice. This legislative referral is not an agency enforcement decision; a final determination was not verified.

Company incident disclosure updated 2026-06-26: unauthorized CRM access was confirmed on 2026-06-17 through a compromised Klue integration. Deel says business contact/commercial data and a limited amount of personal data were affected, not the Deel platform itself; it revoked access and engaged data-protection authorities. Scope and remediation are company statements.
